To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the torque ripple in SynRelM and PM-assisted SynRelMs are lower than in induction motors, but higher than in PMSMs.
the SynRelM is a promising motor topology for low cost high performance electrical drives.
SynRelM and PM-assisted SynRelMs are suitable alternatives to induction motors for applications with high torque ripple and high speed range.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects:
• Synthesis of SynRelMs and PM-assisted SynRelMs with the help of FEA
the design of high-performance low-cost electrical drives, where the SynRelM and PM-assisted SynRelMs are the key components.
a comparative study of SynRelM and PM-assisted SynRelMs with respect to induction and permanent magnet synchronous machines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PM-assisted SynRelMs can replace induction motors and PMSMs in a broad field of applications.
the SynRelM is a good candidate for applications requiring a low cost and high performance motor.
SynRelMs are not suitable for high performance applications but for low cost applications with a high torque ripple and a low average torque.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SynRelMs are a promising alternative to SCIMs for applications where the torque ripple and the average torque is important, e.g. for high performance low-cost electrical drive systems.
SynRelMs can be used as an alternative to SCIMs in low power applications and as an alternative to PM synchronous motors in low power and medium speed applications.
a SynRelM with PMs is a promising alternative to the induction motor for low cost applications, where the speed range is limited to 50% of the rated speed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SynRelMs can be used as a cost effective alternative to induction motors in a broad range of industrial applications.
SynRelMs can be used in a variety of applications and can compete with SCIMs and even PM synchronous machines (PMSMs).

SynRelMs and PM-assisted SynRelMs could offer a good trade-off in terms of performance, cost and reliability for a broad range of applications, especially when high torque density is required at medium to high operating speed.
